# **Interview Log**

This presents the interview logs collected for the project research. The primary objective of these interviews is to gather direct insights from students regarding their experiences, habits, and challenges with buying, selling, or managing unused school materials.

Each log documents the date of the session, the participant's background, the interview method used, and a summary of the responses. These records serve to compile authentic feedback and data to support the project analysis.

| Date | October 21, 2026 |
| :---- | ----- |
| **Role** | 20, Female, 3rd year BS in Information Technology student in MSU-IIT |
| **Method** | Online via Facebook Messenger Chat |

## **Interviewee \#3**

| Date | October 23, 2026 |
| :---- | ----- |
| **Role** | 2nd year Computer Science student |
| **Method** | Face-to-face interview |
| **Q1.** Have you ever bought or tried looking for secondhand school items, like textbooks, lab gowns, or other supplies? | Yes, I did try. It was usually sa mga Facebook groups or Messenger, on pages like MSU-IIT CATS where they sell secondhand items like textbooks, but oftentimes I bought secondhand items directly from people I already know, such as my friends. |
| **Q2.** Can you walk me through the process? What difficulties and concerns did you encounter while buying secondhand items? | I don’t think there are that many concerns, but the only thing I can think of is whether the product is still in good condition. Like when I bought a textbook, I messaged my friend asking if she was available and if the textbook I was looking for was still for sale. I asked her to send a picture of the product so I could check the condition, whether it was still good or not. She sent me the pictures and was honest about the issues, like a small cut, but not that much; it can be fixed easily. |
| **Q3.** Did you encounter any issues regarding time, such as whether you could still get the product on time or whether your schedule aligned with the seller’s? | I didn’t really encounter issues with time, especially on availability, because I chatted with the seller beforehand. Since she is a nursing student and I also have a cousin who is a nursing student, I asked my cousin to inquire about the seller’s available time, to which she replied lunch. Since I was also available during that time, we agreed on it and met on campus at the CEBA building, and I got the product with no issues. |
| **Q4.** Have you experienced this multiple times, buying secondhand items on social media platforms? | Yes, I buy a lot on the Marketplace, especially on the MSU-IIT CATS page, like clothes, and from my cousin also. |
| **Q5.** Have you ever ended up buying a brand-new item because you couldn’t find a secondhand one in time? | Yes, I did. I think it was a lab gown. I originally planned to just borrow from my older sister, but since she was not available and I couldn’t find anything on the Marketplace on time, I just bought a brand-new one. |

## **What have you learned?**

We interviewed one seller (Interviewee \#1) and one buyer (Interviewee \#2) on October 21, 2026\. What she has is a calculator, along with clothes, shoes and containers. She sells by taking photos, writing a caption with details and a meetup location, and posting in several Facebook groups such as MSU-IIT CATS and Iligan Buy and Sell, then waiting for comments or messages. Her posts are sometimes ignored when they get little engagement, and the most frustrating parts are having no interested buyers and waiting for group admins to approve posts. She said categorized listings would convince her to post on our platform, because buyers could go straight to the category she posts in. The buyer said finding an item such as a PE shirt takes 1 to 2 days of checking, roughly 3 to 5 hours in total, because items take long to find and sometimes the seller has not posted yet. He arranges meetups through Messenger, pays by GCash, and hesitates mostly because of item condition and quality.

We interviewed two buyers on October 23, 2026\. Interviewee \#3 buys secondhand items often, mainly from MSU-IIT CATS or from people she knows. Her only concern was condition, so she asked the seller for photos. She also had to message first to find out whether the textbook was still for sale. She once bought a new lab gown after failing to find a secondhand one in time. Interviewee \#4 does not currently look for secondhand items. He had one good experience on Facebook Marketplace with a responsive seller, but he is doubtful about the products because Facebook only acts as a middleman. He also bought a new GEC textbook after finding no good secondhand one.

Interviewee \#5 searches Facebook Marketplace by keyword first, then buy-and-sell groups, and gives up if the item doesn’t show up within a few posts, usually in under an hour. He has bought from physical stores when he couldn’t find an item online. His last used purchase was a phone, paid in cash at a meetup in a crowded place. He inspects items carefully and cancels if he finds undisclosed issues.

Interviewee \#6, a 1st-year nursing student, expects to search Facebook for 30 minutes to an hour daily for next semester’s materials. He bought his books new from the school because searching for secondhand ones was a hassle and the bundle cost less than 500 pesos more. He last bought a uniform from a senior, met on campus and paid in person, and he weighs condition against price. Interviewee \#7 comments on a post, the seller messages her, and they set the meetup and payment. Her main hesitation is the seller possibly being a scammer. Her answer to the question about time spent searching was only “Yes” and does not tell us anything useful.

## **How did it change your proposal?**

The seller’s answers support our assumption that posts get lost in Facebook groups, and they gave us a specific reason she would use a new site: categories. We kept the category field and the browse-by-category feature, and we will make categories prominent on the browse page. The buyer’s concern about condition led us to keep the required photo and condition fields on every listing. This affects Section 3 and Section 5\. We interviewed only one seller, and she did not have the textbooks and lab gowns we expected, so our assumption that seniors have unused materials and will list them still needs more checking.

Both buyers had bought new because they couldn’t find a secondhand item in time, which supports our problem statement. \#3’s need to ask whether an item was still for sale supports our “mark as sold” feature. The condition and photo concerns made us keep the required photo and condition fields. Interviewee \#4’s doubt about the legitimacy of sellers is a trust concern that our scope does not fully address, since we exclude ratings and enrollment verification. Registration with @g.msuiit.edu.ph emails is our only safeguard, so we will note this in our risks.

Interviewee \#5 challenges our assumption that buyers spend a lot of time searching. For him, search is already quick. His answers support the case for keyword search by title and course, and for buying in person with cash on campus, which matches our plan.

Interviewee \#6 shows that buyers will pay more to avoid the hassle of searching, so our platform has to be clearly faster than Facebook. We kept the plan to pre-load real listings and to show condition and price on each listing. Interviewee \#7’s scam concern again points to trust, which we address only through MSU-IIT email sign-in. We did not ask what would make students switch from Facebook, so unanswered question 2 remains open.
